steps.text: Combine ground beef, pork sausage, and sliced pepperoni in a large stockpot over medium heat. Add onions, carrots, celery, bell peppers, and garlic; cook and stir until beef and sausage are browned and crumbly and vegetables are tender. Transfer the mixture into a large colander to drain grease.

Add diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, mushrooms, beef broth, bouillon cubes, oregano, basil, thyme, sugar, bay leaves, pepper, and red pepper flakes to the empty stockpot. Add drained meat mixture and stir until well combined. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Meaty Spaghetti Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This meaty spaghetti sauce recipe is a hearty blend of beef, pork, and pepperoni with tomatoes, peppers, aromatics, and a medley of spices.

review.reviewBody: THE BEST! I was making meatballs so I made this sauce without the meats. I basically followed the recipe; only changes I made were to add additional 1 tablespoon of minced garlic (as garlic lover), add additional 2 (15 oz) cans of tomato sauce (sauce was too thick), add 1 (28 oz) can of pureed tomatoes (sauce was too thick), add additional ½ teaspoon of crushed red pepper flakes (for extra heat), add 2 teaspoons of soy sauce (for flavor and deep color), replace honey for the sugar and add additional 1 tablespoon of honey (for little bit of sweetness). My husband and 8 other guests raved! Easy, simple and delicious! Thanks for the great recipe!

Read reviews first & left out beef bouillon, but the sauce needed the extra flavor. So, I added 3 teaspoons of Better than Bouillon which gave some richness to the sauce without taking away the tomato flavor. I only made a few adjustments based on what I had on hand and suggestions from other reviews. I used a whole red bell pepper and a jalapeno, no mushrooms (but I bet it would have been even better), 1 cup of white cooking wine, and 1 can of tomato paste. My husband was very pleased with this sauce and asked me to make it again- which is rare. I am also glad that the sauce disguises so many vegetables. It's a great way to sneak them in for those people who won't eat them separately. Thank you for the recipe!

I cooked this up and threw everything in the crockpot to simmer on low all day. I used all red pepper (noone in this house likes green pepper), I tripled the garlic (at least), I used all organic canned ingredients, I omitted the carrots and celery (I'm low on ingredients until shopping day). Because I used a double-strength canned beef broth, I did not use the bouillion cubes. I did add a glug of red wine at the last and I used brown sugar instead of white, only because that's what I always do with spaghetti sauce. This turned out really well and seemed to get even better the more it simmered in the crockpot. This made for a hearty spaghetti dinner, easily pulled together out with pantry ingredients plus this made enough for two more large meals later down the road.

Made this last week with a few adjustments for items we did not have on hand: left out ground sausage and pepperoni and used a total of 2.5 lbs 90/10 ground beef. Left out the tomato sauce and tomato paste, and used one 28-ounce can crushed tomatos. Left out the canned mushrooms and red peppers because we also didn't have those. Used 1-tablespoon honey instead of sugar just because. Not mentioned in the recipe, but I salt and peppered the meat and raw veggies after I added them to the pot. Did not use bouillon cubes because I didn't have them, but I used 4t. beef Better than Bouillon and 1-cup of water. I used everything else the recipe called for. Cooked 1 hr 45 minutes with lid on, then removed the lid and cooked another 30-45 minutes to intensify the flavor. Adjusted with salt and fresh ground black pepper in the end, and possibly the best meat sauce I have ever made and eaten. I usually make Mama DiSpirito meatballs with tomato sauce, but this was every bit as good as the giant Italian meatballs. Fabulous, and I highly recommend!

I've used allrecipes.com for a while and I've been looking for the "notes" section it used to have. It's where I made notes to myself on what I did to the recipe so I would remember next time. Since I can't find it, I'm putting it in a "review", but please know, I don't mean to bastardize the recipe, it's just how I happened to make it and I loved it so much I don't want to forget. I had left over roast I wanted to use in a spaghetti sauce, so I used about 2 cups small cubed roast instead of the meats in this recipe. It shredded into small bits when heated which is what I was hoping. I used three 14.5 oz cans diced tomatoes and one 8 oz can tomato sauce. Garlic, celery, onion, yellow pepper. Spices were the same, including bouillon and water, with exception of no red pepper flakes and 1 Tbs agave nectar instead of white sugar. I added 1/2 cup of red wine. Simmered for 2 hours. MMMMMMMMmmmmmmm. So good.

This turned out GOOD!! Mom said that she really likes it and that it has real Taste!! The only thing that I did different is that I used Italian Sausage (Mild) instead of just Pork Sausage and instead of cooking it in a stock pot on the stove for 2 hours, I put it in the Slow Cooker for 6 hours.

very good recipe, lot's of body to it. Takes some time to make though. Started out by sauteed fresh mushrooms in butter, then the garlic and onion in olive oil. placed in a large pot with all the tomato stuff and sugar to start a simmer. browned all the meat, including peperoni, one at a time. added that to the base. then added broth, veggies, herbs and finally the wine. took a about an hour and a half preparing it this way. Adders and substitutions. added a whole peperoni stick 250gm. Used 4 links of medium hot italian sausages without the casings, and about 3/4 lb of ground beef. Used all the spices, as per the recipe. No need to add any salt or pepper. Just great the way it is. Added a cup of red wine, just to round out all those flavours. This one's a keeper!

Great recipe and very close to my own passed down from my Grandmother. Instead of the Celery and Carrots, I pour in some V-8 juice ... saves chopping time. I also don't use as much of the beef elements, i.e. broth or bullion, but otherwise ... Yum! I personally don't like overly sweet tomato gravy. I actually add a little chili powder to knock the edge off of the "sweet".

Amazing! I did mine in a crock pot and it turned out wonderful. If you have picky veggie eaters you can fry up the vegetables and then puree them to put them in the sauce, and it still tastes great. Since discovering this recipe we have NEVER gone back. We refuse to buy sauce now. Thank you for this!

AMAZING!!! I love how many veggies are in this too. I used fresh mushrooms, fresh tomatoes from my garden, added some good red wine, doubled the garlic and also added 1lb ground turkey. 
My mom made this for a big party dinner and I took some home and ate it for lunch and dinner 3 days in a row. Still not sick of it. I'm pregnant and can't handle any meat or veggies right now, so that's saying something! =)

I made this but didn't add carrots because I didn't have any; instead, I used a can of corn and a can of green beans. My family loves it like this! I also grind my mushrooms so small that my kids don't see them, or else they would pick them out.
This is perfect. I've made it as written and with some tweaks. I left off the sugar and the pork, doubled the beef and all of the spices. Perfection either way!

We call your recipe Meatlovers Sauce. Men, children, and the elderly will come back for 2nds and 3rds. No teeth required to enjoy this. I use the entire 6 oz pkg of pepperoni and increased the garlic to taste. Where has this recipe been all my life? My family asks for the pasta that holds the most sauce (rotini)🥰
This is so delicious! It's the only spaghetti sauce I make now. Served it at a fundraiser dinner and it was a big hit!!!!
I put moose meat in instead of hamburger . I substitute the pepperoni with salami. It turned out really delicious my family‘s favourite

BEST.RECIPE.EVER!!! So good I even tried it as a vegetarian option for one of my daughters. I substituted the beef, sausage and pepperoni of course for plant based option. I used vegetable bouillon and broth in place of the beef. I know it's called meaty spaghetti sauce, but this recipe is so much more than the meat. It is absolutely delicious!
Great flavor if you are willing to wait. It takes a long time to prepare.
